title: Fibonacci goes large
prompt:
Compute the `n`th Fibonacci number for the `n` the starter reads. With the 50 in the stdin box the answer is 12,586,269,025, which does not fit in 32 bits, so the loop has to run in `x` registers.

Keep the classic sliding pair: `a` and `b` start as 0 and 1, and `n` times over, the new value is `a + b`, then the pair slides forward. When the loop ends, `a` holds the answer.

## what is checked

- `fib(50)` printed on its own line
- the program exits cleanly
- the loop builds it (answer not written in)
- the same holds for other values of `n` you do not see, from `fib(0)` up to `fib(92)`, the largest that fits in a signed 64-bit register
starter:
// fibonacci numbers grow past 32 bits fast
define(fp, x29)
define(lr, x30)

define(a_r, x19)
define(b_r, x20)
define(next_r, x21)
define(i_r, x22)
define(n_r, x23)

        .data
fmt_in:     .string "%lld"
fmt_out:    .string "fib(%lld) = %lld\n"

        .bss
        .balign 8
n_m:        .skip 8

        .text
        .balign 4
        .global main
main:
        stp     fp, lr, [sp, -16]!
        mov     fp, sp

        ldr     x0, =fmt_in                 // read n
        ldr     x1, =n_m
        bl      scanf
        ldr     x9, =n_m
        ldr     n_r, [x9]

        mov     a_r, 0                      // fib(0)
        mov     b_r, 1                      // fib(1)
        mov     i_r, 0

        // TODO: n times over, advance the pair: the new value is
        // a + b, then a takes b's place and b takes the new value.
        // When the loop ends, a_r holds fib(n).

        ldr     x0, =fmt_out
        mov     x1, n_r
        mov     x2, a_r
        bl      printf

        mov     w0, 0
        ldp     fp, lr, [sp], 16
        ret
